parts.title: My year in Canada
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was sixteen, I spent a year in Canada as an exchange student. I remember the first day very clearly. I stood at the airport with a big suitcase, feeling nervous and excited. My host family, the Parkers, held a sign with my name on it, and they gave me a warm hug.

The first weeks were hard. My English was not as good as I had thought, and in class, I could not follow the teacher. At dinner, my host brother, Jake, talked so fast that I nodded and smiled without understanding. I often went to my room and cried because I missed my family.

Things changed after two months. I joined the school swimming team, and my teammates became my friends. They helped me with my homework, and I taught them some words from my language. One evening, I realised that I had been thinking in English all day.

When I left, the whole family came to the airport. This time, I was the one who was crying. I still write to them every month, and next summer, Jake is coming to visit me.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel at the airport?
questions.explanation: She was nervous and excited.

questions.prompt: What was difficult at first?
questions.explanation: Her English was not as good as she thought, and she could not follow the teacher.

questions.prompt: What helped her to make friends?
questions.explanation: She joined the school swimming team.

options: She will start a new school

parts.title: Tips for living abroad
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Moving to another country is exciting, but it is not always easy. [1] A little preparation can make the first weeks much smoother.

Before you leave, learn some basic words in the local language. [2] People are usually delighted when a foreigner tries to speak their language, even badly.

When you arrive, try to find friends quickly. [3] Join a club or a class, and say yes to every invitation, even if you feel shy.

Be patient with yourself, too. [4] It can take months before you stop feeling like a stranger, and that is quite normal.

Finally, stay in touch with your family at home. [5] But do not spend all your time on the phone, or you will miss the adventure around you.
sentences: A short call every week will make you feel less alone.
Saying hello and thank you will already help.
Banks in most countries are closed on Sundays.
Do not expect to feel at home straight away.
Some of them speak better English than you think.
Nobody knows you on the first day.
The language, the food and even the weather may all be new to you.
Food will always be the biggest problem.

gaps.explanation: Moving is "not always easy" because so much is new; the next sentence says how preparation helps.
Saying hello and thank you will already help; the next sentence says people are delighted when you try.
Nobody knows you on the first day, so find friends; the next sentence says to join a club.
Being patient means not expecting to feel at home straight away; "it can take months" follows.
A short call every week helps; the next sentence says not to spend all your time on the phone.

parts.title: An email to a host family
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Dear Mr and Mrs Parker, Thank you very much for [1] me to stay with you next summer. I am really looking forward to meeting you. I have been learning English for six years, but I am a little worried that I [2] understand everything. I will try to speak slowly, and I hope you [3] mind if I ask you to repeat things. I would like to bring a small present from my country, [4] I do not know what you like. Please tell me if you have any pets, because I am [5] to cats. I arrive on the fifteenth, [6] I will phone you from the airport. Best wishes, Poe

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: After the preposition for we use the -ing form: inviting.

questions.prompt: Gap 2

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: I hope you will not mind: polite request.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: But shows contrast: he wants to bring a present, but does not know what.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: Allergic to is the fixed pattern.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: And joins two pieces of arrival information.

parts.title: Culture shock
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Many people who live abroad experience something called culture shock. At first, everything seems new and exciting. [1] a few weeks, however, small differences begin to feel difficult. The food may taste strange, the weather may be unfamiliar, and people may behave in ways [2] you do not expect. For example, in some countries, it is rude to arrive early, while in others, it is rude to arrive [3] time. You may feel tired, lonely or even angry without knowing why. The good news is that this feeling does not last for ever. Most people start to feel better [4] they make a few friends and learn how things work. Experts say that the best way to deal with culture shock is to stay curious, [5] to laugh at your own mistakes. Remember that millions of people have felt the same, and they have all [6] through it.

gaps.explanation: After a few weeks means once some time has passed.
In ways that you do not expect: relative pronoun.
On time is the fixed phrase for punctual.
Feel better when they make friends: time conjunction.
Stay curious and laugh at mistakes: two pieces of advice.
Got through it means survived a difficult time.

parts.title: A welcome talk for exchange students
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: coordinator
turns.text: Welcome, everybody, to Hillside School. My name is Joni, and I am the coordinator of the exchange programme. This year we have twenty-eight students. At first I thought there would be eleven countries, but two students could not come, so in the end we have nine, from Japan to Brazil. I hope you all had a good journey. Let me tell you about school life. Lessons start every morning at nine. Last year they began at eight, but students said they were too sleepy, so we changed it. The bus from the town centre arrives at half past eight, so you will have time for a coffee. Another good thing is that you do not need to wear a uniform. Some schools ask for one, but not us. Just wear clothes that you feel comfortable in, although in sports lessons you must have special shoes, which you can buy in the shop at the gym. Now, food. Lunch is free for all exchange students in the dining hall, which is on the ground floor. The cafe on the first floor is open too, but you have to pay there, so I suggest the dining hall. Every Thursday afternoon, there are no normal lessons. You can join a club or go on a trip. We used to do this on Wednesdays, but the museum is only free on Thursdays. Please choose your activity on the website this week. Finally, if you have any problem, come and see me. My office is next to the library, on the second floor. Some people look for it near the gym, because the old office was there, but we moved. I’m there from eight till five every day. I hope you enjoy your time with us.

gaps.explanation: She expected eleven countries, but two students could not come, so there are nine.

gaps.prompt: Lessons begin at ___ in the morning
gaps.explanation: Last year lessons began at eight, but now they start at nine.

gaps.prompt: Students are not required to wear a ___
gaps.explanation: Some schools ask for a uniform, but this school does not; only special shoes are needed in sports.

gaps.prompt: Exchange students eat for free in the ___ hall
gaps.explanation: The cafe on the first floor costs money, so lunch is free in the dining hall.

gaps.explanation: They used to be on Wednesdays, but they now take place on Thursdays because the museum is free.

parts.title: An interview with a student who lives abroad
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Bowen, you are seventeen and you have lived in Spain for two years. Why did you move there?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A lot of people think I won a place at a special school, but I didn’t. It was not my idea either, and I never dreamed of an adventure, I was happy in Australia. My mum found a job in Valencia, with a company that makes software, and she said we could go together. I was angry for the first month, I admit. But now I’m very glad.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was the most difficult part at the beginning?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: People expect me to say the language, and yes, the first lessons were hard. But I’d studied Spanish for three years at home, so I could manage. The food was no problem, I love paella. What I found hardest was making friends. Everybody already had their groups, and I sat alone at lunch for weeks. It felt terrible, to be honest.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Did you ever make a big mistake because of the language?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Many! The worst one is funny now. I wanted to go to my cousin’s house, and I said the wrong number to the driver, so I got on the wrong bus. It took me two hours to come back. I didn’t lose my passport and I didn’t miss an exam, just that bus. After that, I always checked the number twice.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Was there a rule that helped you to improve?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Yes, a simple one. My teacher said I should watch Spanish films, or study every evening, but I tried both and neither worked for me. In the end I decided to speak only Spanish at school, even with other foreign students. It was difficult for a month, but my Spanish got better much faster.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you like about the people there?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: They are very friendly, and it’s easy to start a chat with a stranger in the street, but that is not the best thing. The best thing is their patience. When I make a mistake, nobody laughs. People wait, help me find the word, and smile. Everyone is always busy, but they still find time for you.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice would you give to somebody who wants to live abroad?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Be brave and ask questions, all the time. Don’t stay only with people from your own country, that’s comfortable but you learn nothing. And don’t wait until you feel ready, because you will never feel ready. I tried that for a year and I wasted time. Ask, try, make mistakes, and enjoy it.

questions.prompt: Why did Bowen move to Spain?
options: He won a place at a school
His mother found a job there
questions.explanation: He did not win a school place and never wanted an adventure; his mum found a job in Valencia.

questions.prompt: What was the hardest part for Bowen at the beginning?
questions.explanation: He had studied the language and loves the food; what he found hardest was sitting alone at lunch with no friends.

questions.prompt: What mistake did Bowen make?

questions.explanation: He says the worst mistake was taking the wrong bus after giving the wrong number; the passport and the exam were not problems.

questions.explanation: He says to be brave and ask questions, not to stay with people from your country, and not to wait until you feel ready.

parts.title: Getting to know you
parts.instructions: Answer each question in your own words. Aim to speak for 20-30 seconds.

questions.prompt: Would you like to live in another country? Why or why not?
Which languages do you speak or want to learn?
What would you miss most if you lived far from home?
Have you ever met someone from another country? Tell me about it.

parts.title: Describe a photograph
parts.instructions: Look at the photograph and speak for about one minute. Describe what you can see and say what the people might be feeling.
parts.prompt: A group of young people sit and talk together at round tables indoors.

parts.title: Welcoming an exchange student
parts.instructions: Look at the pictures. Talk about the options and decide which one is best.
parts.prompt: Your school is going to welcome an exchange student. Talk about the different things that you could do to help the student feel at home and decide which would be the most useful.

parts.title: Talk about the topic
parts.instructions: Answer the questions. Try to give a reason or an example with each answer.

questions.prompt: Why do people choose to study abroad?
What are the biggest problems of living in a new country?
How can people from different countries understand each other better?
